title: The Powerful Women Who Ruled the Empire
hook: During the 'Sultanate of Women', imperial mothers ruled from palace walls.

scenes.text: Western orientalist paintings depicted the Ottoman imperial harem as a sensual palace prison, but the reality was a political nerve center.

scenes.voicedText: Western orientalist paintings depicted the Ottoman imperial harem as a sensual palace prison, but the reality was a political nerve center.

scenes.text: The harem was an elite academy where hundreds of women received years of education in law, diplomacy, Islamic theology, and calligraphy.

scenes.text: The supreme ruler was the 'Valide Sultan'—the Sultan's mother—who outranked grand viziers and managed astronomical wealth.

scenes.text: During the 16th and 17th centuries, known as the 'Sultanate of Women', matriarchs like Hürrem and Kösem Sultan effectively ran the entire empire.

scenes.text: They corresponded with European monarchs, financed great architectural mosques, and negotiated international peace treaties.
